# Evaluation feedback

1. **Critical — the global hook disables valid Antigravity artifact writes outside Tractor.** `harness/agy/native_write_hook.go:71-95` discards the hook payload and unconditionally denies all three native writers, while `harness/agy/native_write_hook.go:98-112` installs that policy in the user's global `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` and explicitly treats its effect on interactive sessions as a benefit. The primary research instead documents an artifact-aware policy (`deep-research-report-2.md:145-168`): allow targets under the hook payload's `artifactDirectoryPath` and deny targets outside it. The current policy therefore breaks legitimate writes to `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>/`, including normal implementation-plan, walkthrough, and task artifacts, for every manual agy session after Tractor runs. Rework the hook to inspect stdin and allow native writes whose target is contained within `artifactDirectoryPath`, while denying workspace/out-of-root targets. Add unit tests for both decisions and bounded live evidence proving an in-brain native write succeeds and an out-of-brain workspace write is denied. Do not claim global interactive benefit until both paths are demonstrated.

2. **Issue — the delivered design omits the requested manifest, `--agent`, and `init.tools` fail-fast contract.** The invocation at `harness/agy/adapter.go:415-435` never passes `--agent`; the generated stream schema does not expose `init.tools`; and there is no enforcement that rejects advertised native writers or missing `run_command`. 3. **Issue — global hook provisioning can clobber or corrupt user configuration under concurrency or interruption.** `ensureNativeWriteHook` performs an unlocked read-modify-write of the shared global file (`harness/agy/native_write_hook.go:120-156`), and `sync.Once` in `harness/agy/adapter.go:329-345` only serializes one Adapter instance. If global placement remains, use interprocess coordination plus atomic same-directory temp-file/rename semantics (preserving appropriate permissions), and test concurrent merge behavior; otherwise choose a scoped placement that avoids shared persistent user state.

# agy artifact-path bug: preventive layer (round 1)

## TL;DR

The task's hypothesized fix — a custom-agent `tools:` allowlist selected via
`agy --agent <name>` — **does not work**. I proved this empirically with
five real `agy 1.1.15` invocations before writing any adapter code for it,
then pivoted to the mechanism that does work: a global `PreToolUse` deny
hook (`hooks.json`), which is real, documented (inside the CLI binary
itself), and verified live to block the broken tool call before it executes.
It does not eliminate the reactive repair-retry from `ae5edb6` — nothing I
found does, in agy 1.1.15's headless single-turn model — but it converts an
agy-internal, version-fragile failure into a fast, deterministic,
Tractor-controlled one, and the existing repair-retry still recovers the
turn exactly as before. Full reasoning and evidence:
`ephemeral/worklog/202608191900-agy-artifact-prevention.md` (durable,
survives the source research reports being deleted).

## What I built

- `harness/agy/native_write_hook.go` (new): idempotent, merge-safe
  provisioning of a Tractor-owned `PreToolUse` hook entry in agy's global
  `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`, denying `write_to_file`,
  `replace_file_content`, and `multi_replace_file_content` before they
  execute. Collision-safe: refuses to overwrite a same-named hook that
  lacks Tractor's marker string, rather than clobbering a user's own hook.
- `harness/agy/adapter.go`: `ensureHook()` provisions the hook once per
  `Adapter` (`sync.Once`) before the first `agy` invocation.
  `isArtifactPathError` now also matches the hook's own denial text, so
  the existing `ae5edb6` bounded repair-retry catches and recovers from it
  identically to agy's native artifact-path error. `categorize()` gained a
  `"denied by pre-tool hook"` terminal marker so a persistent denial (both
  turns fail) is categorized `ErrorTerminal`, matching the existing
  artifact-path behavior, not `ErrorRetryable`.
- `runnerConfig` gained a `homeDir` override (empty = `os.UserHomeDir()`)
  so tests never touch the real `~/.gemini`. **This was a real bug I found
  and fixed in the test harness itself**: before this change, every
  existing test that called `RunTurn`/`CreateSession` would have silently
  provisioned into the developer's actual global agy config the first time
  this feature landed and tests ran. `testAdapter` now always sets
  `homeDir: t.TempDir()`.

### What I deliberately did NOT build

Per the task's own instruction to verify empirically rather than trust the
reports: I built the `--agent` + custom-agent-manifest + `init.tools`
invariant-enforcement path first, then **tore it out** after proving live
that agy 1.1.15 does not honor a `mainAgent`'s `tools:` allowlist at all —
`init.tools` reports the full 57-tool baseline regardless of the manifest
content (tested down to a 1-tool allowlist), and an explicitly-excluded
`write_to_file` remained fully callable and reproduced the original bug.
Shipping that code anyway would have been dead, misleading infrastructure —
an `--agent` flag and an `init.tools` fail-fast check that either does
nothing or (if implemented as literally specified: fail if `write_to_file`
is advertised) would make **every single turn fail**, since that tool is
always advertised. Full evidence and the manifest shape (kept for future
reference, in case a later agy version fixes this) is in the worklog.

## Placement decision and tradeoffs

**Global** (`~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`), not workspace-local
(`<workdir>/.agents/hooks.json`):

- Tractor's isolated-worktree branches (`engine/artifacts.go`, `2485e4c`)
  each get their own workdir. A workspace-local hook file would need
  provisioning into and cleanup from every branch's worktree, and any file
  left behind would show up in that branch's `git status` and risk being
  swept into artifact collection — exactly what the task said to avoid.
  A single global file, written once, sidesteps both.
- Real tradeoff, accepted deliberately: the hook is global, so it also
  denies native writes for the user's own manual interactive `agy
  --add-dir <workspace>` sessions, not just Tractor-launched ones. Since
  the underlying bug isn't print-mode-specific, this is net-positive — it
  fixes the same failure for their own usage too — but it is a real,
  disclosed behavior change outside Tractor's own runs. Documented in the
  worklog.
- Idempotent and collision-safe: `ensureNativeWriteHook` merges into any
  existing `hooks.json` (doesn't touch other keys), no-ops if its own key
  already matches canonical content byte-for-byte, and errors out rather
  than overwriting a same-named key that isn't Tractor's (no marker string
  in its reason text).

Google documents `"deny"` as a **hard block** that executes before the tool, and `PreToolUse.matcher` supports exact tool names or regexes. `write_to_file` is explicitly listed as a supported matcher target. citeturn20view0turn20view1

A global configuration can be:

`~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`

```json
{
  "no-native-workspace-writes": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "^write_to_file$",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "~/.local/bin/agy-block-native-write",
            "timeout": 5
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

with:

`~/.local/bin/agy-block-native-write`

```sh
#!/bin/sh
cat >/dev/null

printf '%s\n' \
  '{"decision":"deny","reason":"write_to_file is disabled. Use run_command for workspace file creation."}'
```

Hooks are documented under the workspace `.agents/` customization directory or global `~/.gemini/config/`; the CLI changelog also records fixes specifically for workspace-local hooks and for disabled plugin hooks, confirming that this hook framework is part of the CLI customization path rather than only an IDE feature. citeturn20view3turn19view4turn19view2

More interestingly, you can make the rule **artifact-aware** instead of globally disabling the tool. Every hook receives the runtime's actual `artifactDirectoryPath` as well as the mounted `workspacePaths`, so you can allow `write_to_file` only when the target is underneath the brain artifact directory and reject it everywhere else. citeturn20view0

For example, with `jq` available:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

input="$(cat)"
target="$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.toolCall.args.TargetFile // ""')"
artifact_root="$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.artifactDirectoryPath // ""')"

case "$target" in
  "$artifact_root"/*)
    printf '%s\n' '{"decision":"allow"}'
    ;;
  *)
    printf '%s\n' \
      '{"decision":"deny","reason":"write_to_file outside the conversation artifact directory is disabled; use run_command for workspace files."}'
    ;;
esac
```

That is essentially the missing “scope `write_to_file` to artifact storage” policy implemented at the hook layer.

I would still choose the **custom-agent allowlist** first. A hook denies the model *after* it proposes the call, so the agent has to recover from the denial and choose `run_command`; a tool allowlist prevents it from seeing `write_to_file` in the first place. The stream `init.tools` field gives you a particularly clean way to verify the latter invariant. citeturn20view1turn23view4

There is one caveat around `--dangerously-skip-permissions`: official headless documentation says that flag changes the effective permission mode to `always-proceed` and auto-approves tool permission requests, while Hooks documentation describes `PreToolUse` as a separate pre-execution gate whose `"deny"` result hard-blocks execution. I found **no documentation saying `--dangerously-skip-permissions` bypasses hooks**; the documented architecture therefore indicates the hook should still gate the tool, but unlike the `tools:` allowlist I did not find an explicit sentence testing that exact combination. citeturn23view4turn20view1

A third, less attractive option is permission policy. Antigravity's permission language has separate `write_file(...)` and `command(...)` resource actions, and current headless mode respects persisted permissions. Thus, without `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, native writes can be denied while selected shell commands are allowed. However, this acts at the permission layer rather than removing the tool and is therefore inferior for your failure mode. The public API/configuration surfaces, current docs, release history, and issue tracker reveal none. citeturn10view0turn25search2

## What the artifact validator appears to be doing

The strongest clue is in the documented native tool schema itself. Google's Hooks reference describes `write_to_file` as:

```text
write_to_file
  TargetFile
  Overwrite
  CodeContent
  Description
  IsArtifact             optional
  ArtifactMetadata       optional
```

and `multi_replace_file_content` likewise accepts optional `ArtifactMetadata`. citeturn20view0

At the same time, the runtime exposes a dedicated `artifactDirectoryPath`, distinct from `workspacePaths`. citeturn20view0

That makes your failure highly consistent with this sequence:

1. `TargetFile=/workspace/foo.md` is accepted by the ordinary file-write/permission layer because `/workspace` is active through `--add-dir`.
2. The Cortex call also carries artifact semantics — likely `IsArtifact` and/or `ArtifactMetadata`, or is subsequently interpreted as an artifact-bearing call.
3. The permission/declaration converter validates that metadata against the conversation's `artifactDirectoryPath`.
4. The converter discovers that `/workspace/foo.md` is not inside `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<conversation-id>/` and returns `invalid_args`.
5. Because this happens while converting/declarating the model tool call, the otherwise successful filesystem mutation is followed by a failed turn.

Steps 2–4 are an inference from your exact error plus the official tool/hook schemas, rather than publicly inspectable implementation code. The inference is reinforced by 1.1.15's release note: Google fixed artifacts in **subdirectories of “a conversation's artifact directory”** not appearing in the artifact list. That wording strongly confirms that artifact identity remains rooted in one conversation-specific directory; the change permits `brain/<uuid>/scratch/...`, not arbitrary workspace roots. citeturn19view0turn20view0

That 1.1.15 change is important for your case because it means the release shipped **today with artifact-directory work**, but it did not announce workspace artifact roots. I would therefore not expect upgrading from 1.1.14 to 1.1.15 to make `<workspace>/foo.md` a legal artifact. citeturn19view0

The ideal product behavior is probably not to make every `--add-dir` an artifact directory. A cleaner fix would be for ordinary workspace `write_to_file` calls to remain ordinary workspace writes and for the converter to apply `ArtifactMetadata` validation **only when the call is actually declaring an artifact**. The fact that `IsArtifact` is an optional field in the official tool schema makes that separation particularly natural. citeturn20view0

# agy artifact-path bug: preventive layer, and why the documented fix doesn't work

Distillation of two now-deleted research reports
(`deep-research-report-2.md`, primary; `Antigravity CLI Path Configuration.md`,
corroborating) plus five bounded, real `agy 1.1.15` smoke invocations run
during this work, kept here because the source reports will not survive.
Continues [[202608191356-agy-artifact-validator]] (the reactive repair-retry
added in `ae5edb6`), which this work keeps as a fallback layer.

## The failure mechanism

`agy`'s native `write_to_file` (and `replace_file_content`,
`multi_replace_file_content`) physically writes the requested file
successfully, then agy's own end-of-turn bookkeeping — "declaring
permissions", converting the tool call into an artifact-permission record
inside agy's internal `cortex` layer — rejects the target path because it
lies outside agy's private per-conversation
`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>/` directory:

```
declaring permissions: cortex tool write_to_file: convert tool call for
permissions: model output error: invalid tool call error (invalid_args)
<path> is not a valid artifact path; artifacts must be in
~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>/
```

This fails the **whole turn**, discarding structured output along with it,
even though the file is genuinely on disk. `--dangerously-skip-permissions`
does not affect this: it only auto-approves the interactive tool-permission
prompt, a different check from artifact-path validation.

## Why no flag/setting/env var fixes the artifact root

Exhaustively audited (both reports, current as of 2026-08-19): `--add-dir`
scopes filesystem *access*, not the artifact namespace — the CLI's own Hooks
API exposes `workspacePaths` and `artifactDirectoryPath` as distinct fields.
`settings.json`'s `artifactReviewPolicy: "always-proceed"` only skips the
human *review* step; it does not relax path validation. `--mode`,
`--sandbox`, and `--input-format stream-json` (new in 1.1.15) don't touch
tool selection or the artifact root. No `AGY_*`/`GEMINI_*` environment
variable does either. **There is no supported way to make a workspace path
a valid artifact path.** This part of the research holds up; nothing in the
empirical work below contradicts it.

## The documented mitigation, and why it does not work

Google documents a custom-agent `tools:` frontmatter allowlist, selected
with `agy --agent <name>`, as removing tools from an agent's toolset. The
primary report's central recommendation was: define a `mainAgent: true`
custom agent whose `tools:` list omits `write_to_file` /
`replace_file_content` / `multi_replace_file_content`, launch it with
`--agent`, and verify via the `stream-json` `init.tools` field that the
native writers are absent.

**This does not work for a `--agent`-selected mainAgent in real agy
1.1.15.** Five bounded real invocations (model `gemini-3.5-flash-low`,
`--output-format stream-json`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, temp
workspaces under `/tmp`, `timeout 120` on every call) established this
empirically, superseding both reports:

1. **Baseline, no `--agent`**: `init.tools` lists 57 tools, including
   `write_to_file`. This is the canonical tool-identifier set (see below).
2. **`--agent` with a manifest whose `tools:` used `init.tools`-style
   names verbatim**: agy failed immediately (not a hang) with
   `unknown component: tool "X" not found in registry"` for most of
   them — `tools:` validates against a *different, narrower* identifier
   namespace than what `init.tools` reports.
3. **`--agent` with a manifest whose `tools:` used only the subset of
   names that registry-validated cleanly (20 tools, including
   `run_command`, omitting the three native writers)**: the turn
   succeeded, but **`init.tools` still reported the full 57-tool
   baseline, `write_to_file` included** — the allowlist changed nothing
   observable in the reported tool set.
4. **Same manifest, prompt explicitly forcing `write_to_file`**: the model
   called it, and it was **fully executed** — reproducing the exact
   original bug (`... is not a valid artifact path ...`), physical write
   included. The tool was never actually removed from the model's
   capability, regardless of the manifest.
5. **Manifest with `tools: [view_file]` only (nothing else, not even
   `run_command`)**: `init.tools` was unchanged (still all 57), and the
   turn behaved identically to no restriction at all.

Conclusion: for a `--agent`-selected `mainAgent`, agy 1.1.15's `tools:`
allowlist is **inert** — it does not restrict `init.tools` reporting, and
it does not restrict which tools the model can actually call. It is
possible the field only functions for dynamically-defined subagents
(`define_subagent`'s `enable_write_tools`, invoked via `invoke_subagent`),
not for the CLI's `--agent` selection path, but that is inference, not
something re-tested here. **Do not trust the primary report's central
claim without re-verifying against whatever agy version is in use.**

One corroborated detail: the *corroborating* report's warning that an
unrecognized tool identifier in `tools:` can hang the CLI indefinitely did
**not** reproduce here — invocation 2 above failed fast (~1s) with a clear
"not found in registry" error, not a hang. That doesn't mean the risk is
imaginary (it may depend on identifier or agy build), so real smoke tests
under a hard `timeout` remain the right way to validate any future manifest
change, not a substitute for it.

Given this, **Tractor does not provision a custom agent or pass `--agent`.**
It would be dead, misleading infrastructure: code that looks like a
functioning guard but empirically guards nothing. If a future agy version
fixes `tools:` enforcement for mainAgents, this is worth revisiting — the
manifest shape from the primary report is:

```yaml
---
name: <tractor-owned-name>
mainAgent: true
tools:
  - view_file
  - list_dir
  - find_by_name
  - grep_search
  - run_command
  # omit write_to_file, replace_file_content, multi_replace_file_content
---
```

placed at `~/.gemini/config/agents/<name>/agent.md` (global) or
`.agents/agents/<name>/agent.md` (workspace-local), selected via
`agy --agent <name>`. Re-run the same style of empirical smoke test
(invocation 4 above — explicitly force the native writer and see whether it
still executes) before trusting it again.

## Empirically verified tool identifiers (agy 1.1.15, 2026-08-19)

`init.tools` baseline (57 tools; the two reports disagreed with each other
on names like `view_file` vs `read_file` — this is what agy actually
reports):

```
ask_custom_permission, ask_permission, ask_question, browser_click_element,
browser_drag_pixel_to_pixel, browser_get_dom, browser_get_network_request,
browser_input, browser_list_network_requests, browser_mouse_down,
browser_mouse_up, browser_move_mouse, browser_press_key,
browser_refresh_page, browser_resize_window, browser_scroll,
browser_scroll_dom, browser_select_option, browser_subagent,
call_mcp_tool, capture_browser_console_logs, capture_browser_screenshot,
click_browser_pixel, command_status, define_subagent, delete_knowledge,
execute_browser_javascript, find_by_name, finish, generate_image,
grep_search, invoke_subagent, list_browser_pages, list_dir,
list_permissions, list_resources, manage_inbox, manage_subagents,
manage_task, multi_replace_file_content, notebook_edit,
notebook_execution, open_browser_url, read_browser_page, read_resource,
read_url_content, replace_file_content, run_command, schedule,
search_web, sed_file, send_command_input, send_message, view_file, wait,
wait_5_seconds, write_to_file
```

The three native writers Google's Hooks reference documents as
file-mutating (and, for `write_to_file`/`multi_replace_file_content`,
`ArtifactMetadata`-capable): `write_to_file`, `replace_file_content`,
`multi_replace_file_content`. These are the ones the fix targets.
`sed_file` and `notebook_edit` are also plausibly native mutators (new
identifiers neither report named), but weren't independently confirmed to
trip the same bug, so they're intentionally left alone rather than
speculatively blocked.

The `tools:` frontmatter registry (item 2 above) uses a smaller, different
namespace — of the 57, only about 20 validated cleanly, including
`ask_custom_permission`, `ask_permission`, `ask_question`,
`define_subagent`, `find_by_name`, `finish`, `generate_image`,
`grep_search`, `invoke_subagent`, `list_dir`, `manage_subagents`,
`manage_task`, `notebook_edit`, `read_url_content`, `run_command`,
`schedule`, `search_web`, `send_message`, `view_file`, `wait`. This mapping
is undocumented and not worth relying on further since (per above) the
field doesn't functionally restrict anything for a mainAgent anyway.

## The `init.tools` verification invariant — does not apply as conceived

The plan was: parse `init.tools`, fail fast with a clear terminal error if
a native writer is advertised. **This cannot be implemented as a hard
invariant against the current agy version**, because `write_to_file` /
`replace_file_content` / `multi_replace_file_content` are **always**
present in `init.tools` regardless of any manifest, per the empirical
results above. Enforcing "must be absent" as fatal would make every single
turn fail immediately — a total, self-inflicted outage of the harness, far
worse than the bug it replaces. Tractor's `harness/agy` code does not parse
or enforce `init.tools` for this reason. If a future agy version actually
starts honoring `tools:` for mainAgents, this invariant becomes meaningful
again and is worth adding back at that point, gated on a version check.

## What Tractor actually implements: a `PreToolUse` deny hook

agy's lifecycle-hooks system (`hooks.json`, real and documented inside the
CLI binary itself — `strings agy | grep -A200 'Lifecycle Hooks'` dumps the
full spec) supports a `PreToolUse` event that fires **before** a tool
executes and can hard-block it:

```json
{
  "tractor-no-native-write": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "write_to_file|replace_file_content|multi_replace_file_content",
        "hooks": [
          { "command": "<inline shell command>", "timeout": 5 }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The handler receives a JSON context object on stdin (conversation ID,
workspace paths, artifact directory path, tool name/args) and must print a
decision on stdout. Tractor's handler ignores stdin and unconditionally
prints:

```json
{"decision":"deny","reason":"[tractor-no-native-write] Native write_to_file, replace_file_content, and multi_replace_file_content are disabled: agy fails the whole turn when their target lies outside the private brain/<uuid> directory even though the physical write already succeeded. Use run_command for all workspace file writes instead."}
```

**Verified live** (invocation matching this exact hook, forcing
`write_to_file`): the tool call was denied *before* any file touched disk
(`tool_info.state = "ERROR"`, `error.message = "tool call denied by
pre-tool hook: ..."`), and the model correctly recovered by calling
`run_command` instead, which wrote the real file successfully.

**Important limitation, also verified live: this does not prevent the
turn from failing.** Once any tool call in a turn is denied by a
`PreToolUse` hook, agy's `result.status` for the *whole turn* is `ERROR`
with that denial as `result.error` — regardless of the model's successful
recovery afterward. So the hook converts one failure mode (physical write
succeeds, then the turn fails on an agy-internal, version-fragile error
string) into a different, faster, Tractor-controlled failure mode (the
write never happens, the turn fails immediately on a message Tractor
authored and can match reliably) — it does **not** eliminate the burned
turn. Neither documented mechanism (`tools:` allowlist, `PreToolUse` deny)
achieves the "avoid the reactive retry entirely" outcome the original task
hypothesized; that appears not to be achievable in agy 1.1.15's headless
single-turn model at all. The genuine, verified value of the hook is: (a)
deterministic, sub-second failure instead of waiting out a full turn with a
real (and possibly retried-by-the-model) broken write attempt, (b) a
Tractor-controlled, version-stable error signature to match on instead of
depending on agy's exact internal wording, which could change across
releases, and (c) it also fixes the same bug for the user's own manual
interactive `agy --add-dir <workspace>` usage, since the hook is global.

`harness/agy/adapter.go`'s `isArtifactPathError` now matches **either**
signature (agy's own `"is not a valid artifact path"` text, kept as a
fallback in case the hook is ever bypassed, or Tractor's own
`nativeWriteHookMarker`), and the existing bounded repair-retry from
`ae5edb6` handles both identically — one corrective turn instructing
shell-only writes, then propagate on a second failure.

Tractor's isolated-worktree branches (`engine/artifacts.go`, added in
`2485e4c`) each get their own workdir, so a workspace-local file would need
provisioning into and cleanup from every branch's worktree, and any leftover
file would show up in that branch's `git status` and risk being swept into
artifact collection — exactly what this fix must not cause. A global file,
written once, sidesteps both. The tradeoff, accepted deliberately: the hook
also applies to the user's own manual `agy` sessions outside Tractor. Given
the bug it blocks is a genuine defect (not print-mode-specific), this is
net-positive rather than a surprising side effect — but it is a real,
disclosed behavior change to something outside Tractor's own runs.

## Version constraints

Pin **agy 1.1.15+** (`--agent` since 1.1.1, Markdown `agent.md` custom
agents since 1.1.6, `--output-format stream-json` machine-readable tool
events since 1.1.8, `--input-format stream-json` since 1.1.15). Hooks
(`hooks.json`, `PreToolUse`) are present and documented in the 1.1.15
binary; no earlier-version testing was done, so don't assume hooks work on
older builds. The corroborating report's hang-on-unrecognized-tool-identifier
warning applies to the (now-unused) `tools:` allowlist path — since Tractor
doesn't provision a custom agent, this specific risk doesn't apply to
Tractor's current invocations, but keep it in mind if the `tools:` approach
is ever revisited.

## Two-layer design now in Tractor

1. **Prevention** (`harness/agy/native_write_hook.go`): global `PreToolUse`
   deny hook, provisioned idempotently before the first `agy` invocation.
   Blocks the native writers before they execute; does not eliminate the
   turn failure, but makes it fast and deterministic.
2. **Reactive repair** (`harness/agy/adapter.go`, from `ae5edb6`,
   unchanged in spirit): one bounded repair turn, resuming the same
   conversation, instructing shell-only writes — now triggered by either
   the hook's denial or agy's own artifact-path error text. A second
   failure still propagates; no infinite loop.

## Recommended upstream bug reports (`google-antigravity/antigravity-cli`)

**Bug 1 — the original artifact-path defect** (from the primary report,
still not fixed as of 1.1.15):

> **Title**: `write_to_file` succeeds in `--add-dir` workspace, then
> artifact declaration rejects the same path as outside `brain/<uuid>`
>
> **Repro**:
> ```bash
> workspace="$(mktemp -d)"
> agy -p "Create $workspace/foo.md using write_to_file with the contents hello." \
>   --add-dir "$workspace" --dangerously-skip-permissions --output-format stream-json
> ```
>
> **Expected**: either (1) `write_to_file` targeting a path inside an
> active `--add-dir` workspace is treated as an ordinary workspace write,
> no artifact metadata required; or (2) the tool schema prevents
> `ArtifactMetadata`/`IsArtifact` from attaching to non-brain paths; or (3)
> the CLI exposes a documented way to configure the artifact root or
> disable artifact declaration.
>
> **Actual**: the file is written successfully, then the turn fails:
> `declaring permissions: cortex tool write_to_file: convert tool call for
> permissions: model output error: invalid tool call error (invalid_args)
> <workspace>/foo.md is not a valid artifact path; artifacts must be in
> ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>/`

**Bug 2 — new, found during this work: `tools:` allowlist does not
restrict a `--agent`-selected mainAgent.** Google's custom-agent docs
present `tools:` as removing tools from the agent's available set; for a
`mainAgent: true` agent launched via `--agent`, `init.tools` still reports
the full default tool set and an explicitly-excluded tool (tested:
`write_to_file`) remains fully callable. Repro: any of invocations 3–5 in
this doc. Worth filing separately since it invalidates a specific,
publicly-documented capability, not just an edge case.

## Related

- [[202608191356-agy-artifact-validator]] — the reactive repair-retry this
  work sits on top of (`ae5edb6`).

# agy artifact-path bug: preventive layer, and why the documented fix doesn't work

Distillation of two now-deleted research reports
(`deep-research-report-2.md`, primary; `Antigravity CLI Path Configuration.md`,
corroborating) plus real `agy 1.1.15` smoke invocations run across two
rounds of this work, kept here because the source reports will not
survive. Continues [[202608191356-agy-artifact-validator]] (the reactive
repair-retry added in `ae5edb6`), which this work keeps as a fallback
layer. **Round 2** (this revision) replaced round 1's unconditional-deny
hook with an artifact-aware one after independent review found it broke
legitimate in-brain artifact writes, added interprocess-safe provisioning,
added a version-gated runtime invariant for the hook mechanism, and — most
consequentially — found a new agy defect during live re-testing that
materially limits how much either layer actually recovers.

## The failure mechanism

`agy`'s native `write_to_file` (and `replace_file_content`,
`multi_replace_file_content`) physically writes the requested file
successfully, then agy's own end-of-turn bookkeeping — "declaring
permissions", converting the tool call into an artifact-permission record
inside agy's internal `cortex` layer — rejects the target path because it
lies outside agy's private per-conversation
`~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>/` directory:

```
declaring permissions: cortex tool write_to_file: convert tool call for
permissions: model output error: invalid tool call error (invalid_args)
<path> is not a valid artifact path; artifacts must be in
~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>/
```

This fails the **whole turn**, discarding structured output along with it,
even though the file is genuinely on disk. `--dangerously-skip-permissions`
does not affect this: it only auto-approves the interactive tool-permission
prompt, a different check from artifact-path validation.

**Round 2 note:** this failure did not reproduce in several live attempts
this round (see "The sticky conversation-status defect" below) — including
the exact repro command recommended for the upstream bug report. It is not
a deterministic function of "native write to a path outside `--add-dir`
mounted paths"; something about the model's own choice to mark a write as
artifact-bearing (plausibly an `IsArtifact`/`ArtifactMetadata` decision the
model itself makes for content that reads like a deliverable — a plan,
proposal, or report) appears to gate it. This doesn't change the fix (the
hook denies by path, not by intent), but it means the bug is harder to
reproduce on demand than round 1's writeup implied, and no root cause
beyond "these are correlated" was established.

## Why no flag/setting/env var fixes the artifact root

Exhaustively audited (both reports, current as of 2026-08-19): `--add-dir`
scopes filesystem *access*, not the artifact namespace — the CLI's own Hooks
API exposes `workspacePaths` and `artifactDirectoryPath` as distinct fields.
`settings.json`'s `artifactReviewPolicy: "always-proceed"` only skips the
human *review* step; it does not relax path validation. `--mode`,
`--sandbox`, and `--input-format stream-json` (new in 1.1.15) don't touch
tool selection or the artifact root. No `AGY_*`/`GEMINI_*` environment
variable does either. **There is no supported way to make a workspace path
a valid artifact path.** This part of the research holds up; nothing in the
empirical work below contradicts it.

## The documented mitigation, and why it does not work

Google documents a custom-agent `tools:` frontmatter allowlist, selected
with `agy --agent <name>`, as removing tools from an agent's toolset. The
primary report's central recommendation was: define a `mainAgent: true`
custom agent whose `tools:` list omits `write_to_file` /
`replace_file_content` / `multi_replace_file_content`, launch it with
`--agent`, and verify via the `stream-json` `init.tools` field that the
native writers are absent.

**This does not work for a `--agent`-selected mainAgent in real agy
1.1.15.** Five bounded real invocations (model `gemini-3.5-flash-low`,
`--output-format stream-json`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, temp
workspaces under `/tmp`, `timeout 120` on every call) established this
empirically in round 1, superseding both reports:

1. **Baseline, no `--agent`**: `init.tools` lists 57 tools, including
   `write_to_file`. This is the canonical tool-identifier set (see below).
2. **`--agent` with a manifest whose `tools:` used `init.tools`-style
   names verbatim**: agy failed immediately (not a hang) with
   `unknown component: tool "X" not found in registry"` for most of
   them — `tools:` validates against a *different, narrower* identifier
   namespace than what `init.tools` reports.
3. **`--agent` with a manifest whose `tools:` used only the subset of
   names that registry-validated cleanly (20 tools, including
   `run_command`, omitting the three native writers)**: the turn
   succeeded, but **`init.tools` still reported the full 57-tool
   baseline, `write_to_file` included** — the allowlist changed nothing
   observable in the reported tool set.
4. **Same manifest, prompt explicitly forcing `write_to_file`**: the model
   called it, and it was **fully executed** — reproducing the exact
   original bug (`... is not a valid artifact path ...`), physical write
   included. The tool was never actually removed from the model's
   capability, regardless of the manifest.
5. **Manifest with `tools: [view_file]` only (nothing else, not even
   `run_command`)**: `init.tools` was unchanged (still all 57), and the
   turn behaved identically to no restriction at all.

Conclusion: for a `--agent`-selected `mainAgent`, agy 1.1.15's `tools:`
allowlist is **inert** — it does not restrict `init.tools` reporting, and
it does not restrict which tools the model can actually call. It is
possible the field only functions for dynamically-defined subagents
(`define_subagent`'s `enable_write_tools`, invoked via `invoke_subagent`),
not for the CLI's `--agent` selection path, but that is inference, not
something re-tested here. **Do not trust the primary report's central
claim without re-verifying against whatever agy version is in use.**

One corroborated detail: the *corroborating* report's warning that an
unrecognized tool identifier in `tools:` can hang the CLI indefinitely did
**not** reproduce here — invocation 2 above failed fast (~1s) with a clear
"not found in registry" error, not a hang. That doesn't mean the risk is
imaginary (it may depend on identifier or agy build), so real smoke tests
under a hard `timeout` remain the right way to validate any future manifest
change, not a substitute for it.

Given this, **Tractor does not provision a custom agent or pass `--agent`.**
It would be dead, misleading infrastructure: code that looks like a
functioning guard but empirically guards nothing. If a future agy version
fixes `tools:` enforcement for mainAgents, this is worth revisiting — the
manifest shape from the primary report is:

```yaml
---
name: <tractor-owned-name>
mainAgent: true
tools:
  - view_file
  - list_dir
  - find_by_name
  - grep_search
  - run_command
  # omit write_to_file, replace_file_content, multi_replace_file_content
---
```

placed at `~/.gemini/config/agents/<name>/agent.md` (global) or
`.agents/agents/<name>/agent.md` (workspace-local), selected via
`agy --agent <name>`. Re-run the same style of empirical smoke test
(invocation 4 above — explicitly force the native writer and see whether it
still executes) before trusting it again.

## Empirically verified tool identifiers (agy 1.1.15, 2026-08-19)

`init.tools` baseline (57 tools; the two reports disagreed with each other
on names like `view_file` vs `read_file` — this is what agy actually
reports):

```
ask_custom_permission, ask_permission, ask_question, browser_click_element,
browser_drag_pixel_to_pixel, browser_get_dom, browser_get_network_request,
browser_input, browser_list_network_requests, browser_mouse_down,
browser_mouse_up, browser_move_mouse, browser_press_key,
browser_refresh_page, browser_resize_window, browser_scroll,
browser_scroll_dom, browser_select_option, browser_subagent,
call_mcp_tool, capture_browser_console_logs, capture_browser_screenshot,
click_browser_pixel, command_status, define_subagent, delete_knowledge,
execute_browser_javascript, find_by_name, finish, generate_image,
grep_search, invoke_subagent, list_browser_pages, list_dir,
list_permissions, list_resources, manage_inbox, manage_subagents,
manage_task, multi_replace_file_content, notebook_edit,
notebook_execution, open_browser_url, read_browser_page, read_resource,
read_url_content, replace_file_content, run_command, schedule,
search_web, sed_file, send_command_input, send_message, view_file, wait,
wait_5_seconds, write_to_file
```

The three native writers Google's Hooks reference documents as
file-mutating (and, for `write_to_file`/`multi_replace_file_content`,
`ArtifactMetadata`-capable): `write_to_file`, `replace_file_content`,
`multi_replace_file_content`. These are the ones the fix targets.
`sed_file` and `notebook_edit` are also plausibly native mutators (new
identifiers neither report named), but weren't independently confirmed to
trip the same bug, so they're intentionally left alone rather than
speculatively blocked.

The `tools:` frontmatter registry (item 2 above) uses a smaller, different
namespace — of the 57, only about 20 validated cleanly, including
`ask_custom_permission`, `ask_permission`, `ask_question`,
`define_subagent`, `find_by_name`, `finish`, `generate_image`,
`grep_search`, `invoke_subagent`, `list_dir`, `manage_subagents`,
`manage_task`, `notebook_edit`, `read_url_content`, `run_command`,
`schedule`, `search_web`, `send_message`, `view_file`, `wait`. This mapping
is undocumented and not worth relying on further since (per above) the
field doesn't functionally restrict anything for a mainAgent anyway.

## The `init.tools` verification invariant — does not apply as conceived

The plan was: parse `init.tools`, fail fast with a clear terminal error if
a native writer is advertised. **This cannot be implemented as a hard
invariant against the current agy version**, because `write_to_file` /
`replace_file_content` / `multi_replace_file_content` are **always**
present in `init.tools` regardless of any manifest, per the empirical
results above. Enforcing "must be absent" as fatal would make every single
turn fail immediately — a total, self-inflicted outage of the harness, far
worse than the bug it replaces. Tractor's `harness/agy` code does not parse
or enforce `init.tools` for this reason. If a future agy version actually
starts honoring `tools:` for mainAgents, this invariant becomes meaningful
again and is worth adding back at that point, gated on a version check.

Since `init.tools` gives no usable signal, the runtime invariant Tractor
actually enforces for its chosen prevention layer (the `PreToolUse` hook,
below) is a **version gate**, not a tool-set check: `harness/agy` runs
`agy --version` (cheap, no model turn) before trusting a written
`hooks.json` to mean anything, and fails fast if the installed agy is older
than `minSupportedAgyVersion` (`1.1.15`, the only version this hook was
verified live against) or reports a version string that doesn't parse. See
"What Tractor actually implements" below.

## What Tractor actually implements: an artifact-aware `PreToolUse` hook

agy's lifecycle-hooks system (`hooks.json`, real and documented inside the
CLI binary itself — `strings agy | grep -A200 'Lifecycle Hooks'` dumps the
full spec) supports a `PreToolUse` event that fires **before** a tool
executes and can hard-block it:

```json
{
  "tractor-no-native-write": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "write_to_file|replace_file_content|multi_replace_file_content",
        "hooks": [
          { "command": "<inline shell command>", "timeout": 5 }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Round 1 shipped an unconditional deny** — the handler ignored its stdin
payload and always printed `{"decision":"deny", ...}`. Independent review
correctly flagged this as breaking legitimate use: agy's own documentation
(and the primary report) describes the hook's stdin payload as carrying
both the tool call's target and the conversation's real
`artifactDirectoryPath`, meaning a hook *can* distinguish "this is a
genuine artifact write" (which agy's own validator would accept) from "this
is a workspace write mislabeled as an artifact" (the actual bug). An
unconditional deny throws away that distinction and blocks a user's own
interactive `agy` session from ever writing a plan, walkthrough, or task
artifact natively — for no benefit, since the underlying bug only ever
manifests for out-of-brain targets.

**Round 2 (this revision) makes the hook artifact-aware.** The handler
(`nativeWriteHookCommand` in `harness/agy/native_write_hook.go`) reads its
JSON stdin, extracts `artifactDirectoryPath` and every `TargetFile` in the
call's `args`, and allows the call only if every target lies under the
artifact directory; otherwise (or if the payload doesn't parse — fail
closed, not open) it denies with a Tractor-marked reason. The payload
shape and the `TargetFile` field name were captured empirically this round
(not assumed from the reports, which never disagreed on this specific
point but also never gave a full example) — see "Live evidence" below.

The extraction is plain-text (`grep`/`sed`), not a JSON library, so the
hook command stays a single portable POSIX-sh script with no external
interpreter dependency (no `jq`/`python3` assumed on the invoking
machine). `multi_replace_file_content`'s exact `args` shape was **not**
independently captured live this round (budget); the script assumes it
also uses `TargetFile` (Google's Hooks reference groups it with
`write_to_file` as the other `ArtifactMetadata`-capable tool) and denies
any call where that assumption doesn't hold (no `TargetFile` extracted ⇒
deny) — safe by construction, since the failure mode of a wrong assumption
here is an unnecessary deny (recoverable by the repair-retry), never a
wrongful allow.

### Live evidence (round 2)

Captured via a temporary debug hook that logged its own stdin verbatim
before echoing `{"decision":"allow"}`, then confirmed against the actual
Go-generated hook (`ensureNativeWriteHook` against the real `$HOME`,
cleaned up after):

**Hook payload shape** (`write_to_file`, real agy 1.1.15):

```json
{
  "artifactDirectoryPath": "/Users/tyler/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>",
  "conversationId": "<uuid>",
  "modelName": "gemini-3.5-flash-extra-low",
  "stepIdx": 3,
  "toolCall": {
    "name": "write_to_file",
    "args": {
      "TargetFile": "<path>",
      "CodeContent": "...", "Overwrite": true, "Description": "...",
      "toolAction": "...", "toolSummary": "..."
    }
  },
  "transcriptPath": "/Users/tyler/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>/.system_generated/logs/transcript_full.jsonl",
  "workspacePaths": ["<add-dir path>"]
}
```

`replace_file_content`'s payload was also captured live and uses the same
`TargetFile` key (plus tool-specific keys: `Instruction`,
`TargetContent`, `ReplacementContent`, `StartLine`, `EndLine`,
`AllowMultiple`).

**Deny proof, real agy, actual Go-generated hook**: prompted a fresh
conversation to `write_to_file` a workspace path. The tool call's own
`step_update` showed `state: "ERROR"`,
`error.message: "tool call denied by pre-tool hook: [tractor-no-native-write] ..."`;
the target file never appeared on disk; the model's second attempt (a
different workspace path) was denied identically; the turn's
`result.status` was `"ERROR"`.

**Allow proof, real agy, actual Go-generated hook**: resumed that same
conversation (`--conversation <id>`) and prompted a `write_to_file` call
targeting `<that conversation's real artifactDirectoryPath>/allow_test.md`.
The tool call's `step_update` showed `state: "DONE"` with **no** hook
error, and the file was genuinely on disk afterward with the requested
content — proof the artifact-aware hook allows a real in-brain write
through and agy's own validator accepts it, exactly as the artifact-aware
design intends. (The turn's overall `result.status` was still `"ERROR"` —
see the sticky-status defect below; that is a separate, newly discovered
problem, not a failure of the allow path itself.)

## The sticky conversation-status defect (new, round 2)

While proving the allow path above, a resumed turn whose own tool call
**succeeded** (state `DONE`, file correctly written, no per-step error)
still reported `result.status: "ERROR"` at the top level, with `error` set
to the **stale denial text from an earlier turn in the same conversation**.
A follow-up sanity check made this unambiguous: resuming the same
already-denied conversation a *third* time with a prompt that used **no
tools at all** ("Reply with the single word OK.") still returned
`result.status: "ERROR"` with that same stale message, and `num_turns`
kept incrementing (2, then 3) across resumes.

This reproduced identically against both the hand-rolled debug hook and
the real Go-generated `tractor-no-native-write` hook. It was **not**
independently re-confirmed against agy's own native artifact-path error
(as opposed to a hook denial) this round — the exact repro from the
"Upstream bug to file" section below did not reproduce the native error at
all in three attempts (see the failure-mechanism note above), so there was
no live native failure available to resume past. Given both failures
surface through the same conversation-level "declaring permissions /
denied" bookkeeping, it is likely the same defect affects both, but that
inference wasn't independently verified.

**Why this matters for Tractor's design:** `harness/agy`'s
`CreateSession`/`RunTurn` model is explicitly multi-turn — one session ID
is resumed across many `RunTurn` calls over a pipeline run's lifetime,
including the existing `ae5edb6` repair-retry, which resumes the **same**
conversation for its one corrective turn and requires that turn's
`result.status` to come back `"SUCCESS"`. If agy's top-level status is
sticky at the conversation level once any tool-call denial occurs
anywhere in that conversation's history, then:

- The repair-retry's corrective turn, even if the model behaves perfectly
  and writes every file via `run_command` as instructed, is likely to
  **still** report `result.status: "ERROR"` with the original stale
  message — meaning `RunTurn` returns a terminal failure on the "repaired"
  turn, not a recovered result. This was not proven end-to-end against
  the exact `ae5edb6` repair path (that would need reproducing the
  original native artifact-path error live, which didn't happen this
  round), but it follows directly from the sticky-status evidence above,
  which used the identical resume mechanism (`--conversation <id>`).
- Any session that ever attempts one denied native write is plausibly
  **poisoned for the rest of its lifetime** — every subsequent `RunTurn`
  in that session, regardless of what it actually does, would report a
  terminal failure once `result.status != "SUCCESS"` short-circuits
  `harness/agy/adapter.go`'s result handling before it ever looks at
  `structured_output`.
- This makes **prevention** (stopping the denial from ever happening) far
  more valuable than the repair-retry, and means the repair-retry's
  practical recovery rate against real agy 1.1.15 is now in real doubt —
  contradicting round 1's more optimistic framing, which only verified a
  denial recovering **within a single turn** (the model called
  `run_command` after a same-turn denial) and never tested a **separate,
  resumed** repair turn against real agy.

This round did not change `adapter.go`'s repair-retry logic (kept exactly
as `ae5edb6` left it, per the task's explicit instruction), because fixing
it (e.g., abandoning the poisoned conversation and starting a new one,
losing context, for the repair turn) is a larger design change that needs
its own live validation. Flagging it here as the most important open
question for whoever picks this up next.

### Provisioning: global, not workspace-local

`~/.gemini/config/hooks.json`, merged (not replaced) — `ensureNativeWriteHook`
only ever reads/writes its own `"tractor-no-native-write"` key, via
`sync.Once` per `Adapter` before its first `agy` invocation (gated behind
the version check above). Idempotent (re-provisioning with identical
content is a byte-for-byte no-op) and collision-safe (refuses to overwrite
a same-named key that lacks Tractor's marker string in its reason text,
rather than clobbering a user's own hook of the same name).

Global over workspace-local (`<workdir>/.agents/hooks.json`) for the same
reason the (ultimately unused) custom-agent manifest would have needed it:
Tractor's isolated-worktree branches (`engine/artifacts.go`, added in
`2485e4c`) each get their own workdir, so a workspace-local file would need
provisioning into and cleanup from every branch's worktree, and any leftover
file would show up in that branch's `git status` and risk being swept into
artifact collection — exactly what this fix must not cause. A global file,
written once, sidesteps both.

Because the hook is now artifact-aware rather than an unconditional deny,
sharing it globally with the user's own manual `agy` sessions is no longer
a disclosed regression traded for Tractor's benefit — it applies the same
correct policy (allow genuine artifact writes, deny mislabeled workspace
writes) everywhere the hook is active. That said, this round did not
independently re-verify the "benefits interactive use" framing beyond the
two live proofs above; it is a reasonable inference from the design, not a
separately tested claim.

**Concurrency safety (new, round 2):** `ensureNativeWriteHook`'s
read-modify-write is guarded by an exclusive `flock` (via
`golang.org/x/sys/unix`) on a sibling `.tractor-hooks.lock` file, and the
write itself lands via a same-directory temp file plus `os.Rename` (atomic
on the POSIX filesystems agy's config lives on). This closes two gaps
independent review found in round 1: two concurrent Tractor processes (or
a person hand-editing `hooks.json` at the same moment) can no longer both
read the same old document and have the second writer silently discard the
first writer's key, and a crash mid-write can no longer leave a truncated
`hooks.json` (the rename is atomic; a half-written temp file is simply
orphaned, never observed by a reader). Tested with a real concurrency test
(`TestEnsureNativeWriteHookConcurrentProvisioningLosesNoUpdates`, run under
`-race`): several goroutines calling `ensureNativeWriteHook` race against
several more each adding a distinct foreign key via the identical
lock-then-atomic-rename discipline; the test asserts every key from every
writer survives.

### Runtime invariant (new, round 2)

Independent review correctly noted that round 1 wrote `hooks.json` and
then silently trusted it worked, with no invariant confirming the
mechanism was actually supported. `Adapter.ensureHook` now runs
`agy --version` once (cheap, no model turn, same `sync.Once` as hook
provisioning) and requires it to parse as `>= minSupportedAgyVersion`
(`1.1.15`) before writing anything to `hooks.json`. An older or
unparseable version fails the adapter fast with a terminal error naming
the check, the reported version, and the minimum verified version — rather
than proceeding on an unverified assumption. This is deliberately a
**version gate**, not a functional self-test (spending a real model turn
just to prove the hook works would be expensive and would itself be
vulnerable to the sticky-status defect above); it trades "guaranteed
correct" for "cheap and know when the assumption might not hold."

## Version constraints

Pin **agy 1.1.15+** (`--agent` since 1.1.1, Markdown `agent.md` custom
agents since 1.1.6, `--output-format stream-json` machine-readable tool
events since 1.1.8, `--input-format stream-json` since 1.1.15). Hooks
(`hooks.json`, `PreToolUse`) are present and documented in the 1.1.15
binary and now enforced at runtime via the version gate above; no
earlier-version testing was done, so don't assume hooks work on older
builds. The corroborating report's hang-on-unrecognized-tool-identifier
warning applies to the (unused) `tools:` allowlist path — since Tractor
doesn't provision a custom agent, this specific risk doesn't apply to
Tractor's current invocations, but keep it in mind if the `tools:`
approach is ever revisited.

## Two-layer design now in Tractor

1. **Prevention** (`harness/agy/native_write_hook.go`): global,
   artifact-aware `PreToolUse` hook, provisioned idempotently and
   concurrency-safely before the first `agy` invocation, gated on a live
   `agy --version` check. Allows genuine in-brain artifact writes; denies
   native writes targeting anything else, before they execute.
2. **Reactive repair** (`harness/agy/adapter.go`, from `ae5edb6`,
   unchanged in spirit): one bounded repair turn, resuming the same
   conversation, instructing shell-only writes — triggered by either the
   hook's denial or agy's own artifact-path error text. A second failure
   still propagates; no infinite loop. **Its real-world recovery rate
   against agy 1.1.15 is now in doubt** per the sticky conversation-status
   defect above — kept as instructed, not re-designed this round.

## Recommended upstream bug reports (`google-antigravity/antigravity-cli`)

**Bug 1 — the original artifact-path defect** (from the primary report,
still not fixed as of 1.1.15, and still not independently reproduced
on-demand — see the round-2 note under "The failure mechanism"):

> **Title**: `write_to_file` succeeds in `--add-dir` workspace, then
> artifact declaration rejects the same path as outside `brain/<uuid>`
>
> **Repro**:
> ```bash
> workspace="$(mktemp -d)"
> agy -p "Create $workspace/foo.md using write_to_file with the contents hello." \
>   --add-dir "$workspace" --dangerously-skip-permissions --output-format stream-json
> ```
>
> **Expected**: either (1) `write_to_file` targeting a path inside an
> active `--add-dir` workspace is treated as an ordinary workspace write,
> no artifact metadata required; or (2) the tool schema prevents
> `ArtifactMetadata`/`IsArtifact` from attaching to non-brain paths; or (3)
> the CLI exposes a documented way to configure the artifact root or
> disable artifact declaration.
>
> **Actual**: the file is written successfully, then the turn fails:
> `declaring permissions: cortex tool write_to_file: convert tool call for
> permissions: model output error: invalid tool call error (invalid_args)
> <workspace>/foo.md is not a valid artifact path; artifacts must be in
> ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<uuid>/`
>
> **Round-2 caveat**: this exact repro command did not reproduce the
> failure live this round (ran clean, `status: "SUCCESS"`). File the
> report with the original recorded transcript from round 1 as the
> primary evidence, and note that the trigger condition appears
> non-deterministic or content-dependent, not a fixed function of "any
> write to an `--add-dir` path."

**Bug 2 — `tools:` allowlist does not restrict a `--agent`-selected
mainAgent.** Google's custom-agent docs present `tools:` as removing
